page: Microsoft Azure E112ibs_v5 is an isolated virtual machine instance belonging to the EIBSv5 family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 112 virtual CPUs mapped to 56 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 6.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on external block storage and premium storage capabilities.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core and memory performance. The multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmark scored 108538.83, placing it in the top 25% tier, while the single-core stress-ng score of 1899.69 is in the average range. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, reaching 5839.55 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 335.8 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic capabilities are highly efficient, as evidenced by a top-tier PassMark CPU encryption score of 94803.53.

Given its high memory capacity and strong multi-threaded performance, the E112ibs_v5 is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and large-scale web serving. PassMark database operations scored 30672.16, and Redis SET operations achieved 96.47 million operations per second. However, single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, fall into the average performance tier. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for local-disk-heavy tasks or hardware-accelerated machine learning training, though it handles small to medium LLM inference at average speeds.
